Series::unwrap¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signatures¶

Series Series::unwrap() const
Series Series::unwrap(double discont) const
Series Series::unwrap(double discont, std::int64_t dim) const

Recovering A Continuous Phase Path¶

Wrapped phase is commonly reported in a principal interval even when the underlying angle evolves continuously. That representation creates apparent jumps near a full turn. unwrap() removes those artificial jumps by adding integer multiples of 2*pi along one axis while preserving genuine local movement.

For adjacent values with difference delta, the method finds the congruent difference in [-pi, pi] and accumulates the required multiple of 2*pi into all subsequent lanes. Differences smaller than discont are left alone. A positive boundary difference of exactly pi remains positive rather than being changed to -pi.

The overloads mean:

Call

Discontinuity threshold

Axis

unwrap()

pi

Final axis

unwrap(discont)

Caller supplied

Final axis

unwrap(discont, dim)

Caller supplied

Caller selected; negative axes are accepted

Choosing discont < pi does not force corrections for smaller jumps: a jump must still have a shorter complement across the 2*pi boundary. Choosing a value greater than pi suppresses corrections until that larger threshold is crossed. discont must be finite and non-negative.

Shape, Dtype, Empty Inputs, And Reverse Mode¶

The receiver must have at least one axis. Floating and integral inputs are accepted; integral values are promoted to float64 because the correction contains pi. Complex inputs are rejected. Shape and platform are preserved. An empty selected axis returns an empty Series of the resolved floating dtype.

The chosen wrap count is discrete. Away from wrap-decision boundaries, adding a constant multiple of 2*pi has derivative one, so reverse mode passes each output sensitivity to the corresponding input lane. At a discontinuity decision boundary the mathematical operation is not differentiable; the recorded piecewise branch is used.

Examples¶

1. Unwrap the final axis with the default threshold¶

const auto phase =
    pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, -2.0, 0.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, phase.unwrap());

Output¶

Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 1.0000, 2.0000, 4.0000, 4.2832, 6.2832]

The transition from 4 to -2 is interpreted as a short positive movement across the wrap boundary, so one full turn is added from that point onward.

2. Show why a threshold below pi has no extra effect¶

pluss::series::print(std::cout, phase.unwrap(0.5));

Output¶

Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 1.0000, 2.0000, 4.0000, 4.2832, 6.2832]

Although several ordinary differences exceed 0.5, only differences with a shorter modulo-2*pi complement are corrected.

3. Preserve a large jump deliberately¶

pluss::series::print(std::cout, phase.unwrap(7.0));

Output¶

Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 1.0000, 2.0000, 4.0000, -2.0000, 0.0000]

The apparent six-radian jump is below the requested discontinuity threshold, so it is treated as intentional.

4. Select a non-final axis¶

const auto matrix = pluss::make_series({{0.0, 4.0}, {0.0, -4.0}});
pluss::series::print(
    std::cout, matrix.unwrap(3.141592653589793, 0));

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 0.0000 4.0000 ⎤
⎣ 0.0000 2.2832 ⎦

Each column is an independent path because axis zero is selected. The first column needs no correction; the second crosses its boundary.

5. Correct jumps spanning more than one full turn¶

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout, pluss::make_series({0.0, 13.0, -13.0}).unwrap());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 0.4336, -0.4336]

The correction is not limited to one turn. It chooses the required integer multiple of 2*pi for each adjacent difference.

6. Promote integral phase samples¶

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout, pluss::make_series({0, 4, -2}).unwrap());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, -2.2832, -2.0000]

Promotion prevents the irrational turn correction from being truncated back to integers.

7. Differentiate through the selected branch¶

auto tracked = phase.clone();
tracked.tracks_slope_(true);
tracked.unwrap().sum().reverse();
pluss::series::print(std::cout, tracked.sensitivity());

Output¶

Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000]

8. Preserve an empty selected axis¶

const auto empty =
    pluss::series::empty({0}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, empty.unwrap());

Output¶

Series(shape=[0], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=0, contiguous=true)
[]

9. Reject a scalar receiver¶

try {
  (void)pluss::make_series(1.0).unwrap();
} catch (const std::exception& error) {
  std::cout << error.what() << '\n';
}

Output¶

unwrap: dim out of range

A scalar has no axis along which adjacent phase samples can be compared.

Performance¶

The operation performs one sequential accumulation along each selected-axis path and parallelizes naturally across the remaining coordinates. Work and new storage are linear in numel(). Choose the axis that already represents the physical sample order; sorting or permuting phase samples after unwrapping changes the problem rather than merely its layout.

See Also¶

  • angle() obtains wrapped phase from complex values.

  • diff() computes adjacent differences without cumulative turn correction.
